title: The Serum Run

slides.title: ONE DOG GOT A STATUE. THE OTHER GOT FORGOTTEN.

slides.text: Togo ran the longest, most dangerous leg of the relay across frozen sea ice, then passed the medicine on.
Musher Gunnar Kaasen and his lead dog Balto took the final leg, through a blizzard so thick Kaasen couldn't see his own dogs.
Balto kept to the trail. At 5:30 a.m. on 2 February 1925, the team pulled into Nome.
About 1,085 km (674 miles) in five and a half days. The medicine arrived frozen, but it still worked. The outbreak was stopped.
Balto became a celebrity. That same year, New York put a statue of him in Central Park. It is still there today.
Togo, who ran the longest leg, got little credit at the time. Seppala never stopped saying Togo was the real hero.
